Non-local symmetries of the Hirota-Satsuma coupled KdV system and their applications

Junchao Chen Address:  Shanghai Key Laboratory of Trustworthy Computing, East China Normal University, Shanghai, 200062, People’s Republic of China    Xiangpeng Xin Address:  Shanghai Key Laboratory of Trustworthy Computing, East China Normal University, Shanghai, 200062, People’s Republic of China    Yong Chen Email: ychen@sei.ecnu.edu.cn Corresponding author: Corresponding author. Shanghai Key Laboratory of Trustworthy Computing, East China Normal University, Shanghai, 200062, People’s Republic of China Address:  Shanghai Key Laboratory of Trustworthy Computing, East China Normal University, Shanghai, 200062, People’s Republic of China
Abstract

The nonlocal symmetry is derived from the known Darboux transformation (DT) of the Hirota-Satsuma coupled KdV (HS-cKdV) system, and infinitely many nonlocal symmetries are obtained by introducing some internal parameters. By extending the HS-cKdV system to an auxiliary system with five dependent variables, the prolongation is found to localize the nonlocal symmetry related to the DT. Base on the enlarged system, the finite symmetry transformations and similarity reductions about the local symmetries are computed, which lead to some novel exact solutions of the HS-cKdV system. These solutions contain some new solutions from old ones by the finite symmetry transformation and exact interaction solutions among solitons and other complicated waves including periodic cnoidal waves and Painlevé waves through similarity reductions. Some integrable models from the nonlocal symmetry related to the DT are obtained in two aspects: the negative HS-cKdV hierarchy obtained by introducing the internal parameter and integrable models both in lower and higher dimensions given by restricting the symmetry constraints.

1 Introduction

Symmetry study is always a powerful method in physics and other natural and applied sciences, especially, in integrable systems and solion theory [1, 2]. For one known symmetry of a differential system, there are some important applications, such as obtaining new solutions from old ones via corresponding finite transformation [1, 2, 3], reducing dimensions of differential system by similarity reductions [1, 2, 4, 5, 6] and getting new integrable hierarchies and higher dimensional integrable models from original integrable models [7, 8, 9, 10] and so on. A lot of work has devoted to finding the general Lie symmetry by using the classical or nonclassical Lie group method in the past years. However, since it is still challengeable to seek nonlocal symmetries for a given differential system [11, 12, 13], only a few papers have paid attention to the relevant research. Most recently, some efficient techniques for searching nonlocal symmetries of differential equations have been proposed and developed. For example, one can obtained infinite many nonlocal symmetries by recursion operators and their inverses [13, 14, 15, 16, 17], the conformal invariant form (Schwartz form) [9, 10], Darboux transformation (DT) [18, 19, 20, 21], Bäcklund transformation [22], pseudopotentials [3] and potential system [2] and so on.

However, the finite symmetry transformations and similarity reductions cannot be directly calculated from the nonlocal symmetry. This fact leads to few works to construct explicit solutions for the related differential equation(s) in this aspect. Fortunately, the localization of nonlocal symmetry through introducing potential [2] and pseudopotential-type [23, 24, 25] symmetries which possess close prolongation extends the applicability of symmetry method to obtain some new solutions of differential equations. Base on this method, new finite symmetry transformations can be derived (for example, the finite symmetry transformations obtained from DT and the initial DT are different but possess same infinitesimal form [20]) and the original equation(s) need to be expanded into some prolonged systems [3, 20, 22]. Further, to solve these prolonged systems generates some novel exact interaction solutions among solitons and other complicated waves including periodic cnoidal waves and Painlevé waves [20, 22]. Practically, these novel solutions unearthed have potentially important applications in some physical fields [26, 27, 28].

Moreover, to find new integrable models is another important application of symmetry study. For (1+1)-dimensional integrable model, the recursion operator [29, 30, 31] is a valid method to produce the integrable hierarchy. Very recently, Lou [14, 15, 16, 17] has extended some negative hierarchy through utilizing the inverse recursion operator for (1+1)-dimensional integrable models and introducing some internal parameters for (2+1)-dimensional integrable models [10]. In addition, making use of the nonlinearization of Lax pair under certain constraints between potentials and eigenfunctions, Cao has developed a systematic approach to find finite-dimensional integrable systems [32, 33, 34]. In particular, it has also been pointed that by restricting a symmetry constraint to the Lax pair of the soliton equation, one can not only obtain the lower dimensional integrable models from higher ones, but can also embed the lower ones into higher dimensional integrable models [9, 19, 35].

In this paper, we concentrate on the nonlocal symmetry of the Hirota-Satsuma coupled KdV (HS-cKdV) system and their applications. Firstly, the nonlocal symmetry is derived from the known DT of the HS-cKdV system, and infinitely many nonlocal symmetries are obtained by introducing some internal parameters. The prolongation of the nonlocal symmetry related to the DT is found by extending the HS-cKdV system to an auxiliary system with five dependent variables. Then, the finite symmetry transformations and similarity reductions about the corresponding local symmetries are computed for giving novel exact solutions of the HS-cKdV system. These solutions contain some new solutions from old ones by the finite symmetry transformations and exact interaction solutions among solitons and other complicated waves including periodic cnoidal waves and Painlevé waves by similarity reductions. The another work of the paper is to extend the HS-cKdV system to some new integrable models from the nonlocal symmetry related to the DT in two aspects: the negative HS-cKdV hierarchy obtained by introducing the internal parameter and some other integrable models both in finite and infinite dimensions given by restricting the symmetry constraints.

The HS-cKdV system

ut=12​ux​x​x+3​u​ux−6​v​vx,\displaystyle u_{t}=\frac{1}{2}u_{xxx}+3uu_{x}-6vv_{x}, (1.1)
vt=−vx​x​x−3​u​vx,\displaystyle v_{t}=-v_{xxx}-3uv_{x}, (1.2)

is proposed as the coupled KdV system by Hirota and Satsuma, which describes interactions of two long waves with different dispersion relations [36]. In a following paper [37], these authors shown that this coupled KdV system is the four-reduction of the celebrated KP hierarchy and its soliton solutions can be derived from ones of the KP equation. Meanwhile, Wilson [38] observed that the HS-cKdV system is just an example of many integrable systems arose from the Drinfeld-Sokolov theory [39, 40]. Some significant properties of the HS-cKdV system have been revealed in the past years. For instance, the HS-cKdV system possesses bilinear form [36, 41], Lax pair [42, 47, 48], Ba¨{\rm\ddot{a}}cklund transformations [43], Darboux transformations [44, 45, 46], Painleve´{\rm\acute{e}} property [47, 48], infinitely many symmetries and conservation laws [29] etc.

The paper is organized as follows. In Sec.II, the nonlocal symmetry is derived from the DT of the HS-cKdV system, and more nonlocal symmetries can be produced from one seed symmetry through introducing some inner parameters. A prolonged system to localize the nonlocal symmetry is presented by extending the HS-cKdV system. The finite symmetry transformations of prolonged local symmetries and similar reductions of the prolonged system are presented, and some new exact solutions of the original system are obtained. Section III is devoted to finding the negative HS-cKdV hierarchy by introducing the internal parameter and integrable models both in lower and higher dimensions by restricting the symmetry constraints. The last section are conclusions and discussions.

2 Non-local symmetries via Darboux transformation

It is known that DT is the most direct and yet elementary approach for the construction of exact solutions. Using this method, one can obtain new solutions fron old solutions through simple iteration. In this section, we use the invariant properties of differential equations exhibited by DT to deduce the nonlocal symmetries of the HS-cKdV system (1.1)-(1.2).

The Lax pair for the HS-cKdV system (1.1)-(1.2) reads [42, 47, 48]

ψ1​x​x\displaystyle\psi_{1xx} =\displaystyle= −(u+v)​ψ1−λ​ψ2,\displaystyle-(u+v)\psi_{1}-\lambda\psi_{2}, (2.1)
ψ2​x​x\displaystyle\psi_{2xx} =\displaystyle= −(u−v)​ψ2+λ​ψ1,\displaystyle-(u-v)\psi_{2}+\lambda\psi_{1}, (2.2)
ψ1​t\displaystyle\psi_{1t} =\displaystyle= −12​(ux−2​vx)​ψ1+(u−2​v)​ψ1​x−2​λ​ψ2​x,\displaystyle-\frac{1}{2}(u_{x}-2v_{x})\psi_{1}+(u-2v)\psi_{1x}-2\lambda\psi_{2x}, (2.3)
ψ2​t\displaystyle\psi_{2t} =\displaystyle= −12​(ux+2​vx)​ψ2+(u+2​v)​ψ2​x+2​λ​ψ1​x,\displaystyle-\frac{1}{2}(u_{x}+2v_{x})\psi_{2}+(u+2v)\psi_{2x}+2\lambda\psi_{1x}, (2.4)

where {u,v}\{u,v\} is a solution of Eqs.(1.1)-(1.2) and λ\lambda is a spectral parameter.

In Ref.[45, 46], Hu and Liu had constructed the DT for the HS-cKdV system from singularity analysis and reduction of a binary DT. We rewrite it here.

u¯=u+2​(ln⁡θ)x​x,v¯=v+ψ2​ψ1​x−ψ1​ψ2​xθ,\bar{u}=u+2(\ln\theta)_{xx},\ \ \bar{v}=v+\frac{\psi_{2}\psi_{1x}-\psi_{1}\psi_{2x}}{\theta}, (2.5)

θx=ψ1​ψ2,θt=2​λ​(ψ12−ψ22)−2​ψ1​x​ψ2​x−u​ψ1​ψ2.\theta_{x}=\psi_{1}\psi_{2},\ \ \theta_{t}=2\lambda(\psi^{2}_{1}-\psi^{2}_{2})-2\psi_{1x}\psi_{2x}-u\psi_{1}\psi_{2}. (2.6)

and ∂n1+n2∂λ1n1​∂λ2n2​σ​(λ1,λ2)\frac{\partial^{n_{1}+n_{2}}}{\partial\lambda_{1}^{n_{1}}\partial\lambda_{2}^{n_{2}}}\sigma(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}) are also symmetries of the HS-cKdV system (1.1)-(1.2).

3 Localization of the non-local symmetry and exact solutions

3.1 Localization of the non-local symmetry from DT

In this section, we devote to study the symmetry from DT given by Eq.(2.23) in above section. First, we rewrite it as

σu=−2​ψ1​ψ2​x−2​ψ2​ψ1​x,σv=ψ1​ψ2​x−ψ2​ψ1​x,\sigma^{u}=-2\psi_{1}\psi_{2x}-2\psi_{2}\psi_{1x},\ \ \sigma^{v}=\psi_{1}\psi_{2x}-\psi_{2}\psi_{1x}, (3.1)

which apparently contain derivative terms ψ1​x\psi_{1x} and ψ2​x\psi_{2x}. Hence, by introducing new dependent variables φ1≡φ1​(x,t)\varphi_{1}{\equiv}\varphi_{1}(x,t) and φ2≡φ2​(x,t)\varphi_{2}{\equiv}\varphi_{2}(x,t) with

φ1=ψ1​x,φ2=ψ2​x,\varphi_{1}=\psi_{1x},\ \ \ \varphi_{2}=\psi_{2x}, (3.2)

the above symmetry (3.1) is converted into

σu=−2​ψ1​φ2−2​ψ2​φ1,σv=ψ1​φ2−ψ2​φ1.\sigma^{u}=-2\psi_{1}\varphi_{2}-2\psi_{2}\varphi_{1},\ \ \sigma^{v}=\psi_{1}\varphi_{2}-\psi_{2}\varphi_{1}. (3.3)

In the following, we shall list the linearized equations of Eqs. (2.1)-(2.2) and (3.2) with λ=0\lambda=0,

σx​xψ1+(u+v)​σψ1+(σu+σv)​ψ1=0,\displaystyle\sigma^{\psi_{1}}_{xx}+(u+v)\sigma^{\psi_{1}}+(\sigma^{u}+\sigma^{v})\psi_{1}=0,
σx​xψ2+(u−v)​σψ2+(σu−σv)​ψ2=0,\displaystyle\sigma^{\psi_{2}}_{xx}+(u-v)\sigma^{\psi_{2}}+(\sigma^{u}-\sigma^{v})\psi_{2}=0, (3.4)
σxψ1−σφ1=0,σxψ2−σφ2=0.\displaystyle\sigma^{\psi_{1}}_{x}-\sigma^{\varphi_{1}}=0,\ \ \sigma^{\psi_{2}}_{x}-\sigma^{\varphi_{2}}=0.

where σu\sigma^{u} and σv\sigma^{v} is given by (3.3) and σψ1,σψ2,σφ1\sigma^{\psi_{1}},\sigma^{\psi_{2}},\sigma^{\varphi_{1}} and σφ2\sigma^{\varphi_{2}} denote the symmetries of ψ1,ψ2,φ1\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\varphi_{1} and φ2\varphi_{2}, respectively.

Observing from Eq.(2.1) and (2.2), one can easily deduce that solution of (3.4) has the form:

σψ1=p​ψ1,σψ2=p​ψ2,\displaystyle\sigma^{\psi_{1}}=p\psi_{1},\ \ \sigma^{\psi_{2}}=p\psi_{2}, (3.5)
σφ1=ψ12​ψ2+p​φ1,σφ2=ψ1​ψ22+p​φ2.\displaystyle\sigma^{\varphi_{1}}=\psi^{2}_{1}\psi_{2}+p\varphi_{1},\ \ \sigma^{\varphi_{2}}=\psi_{1}\psi^{2}_{2}+p\varphi_{2}. (3.6)

where p≡p⁡(x,t)p{\equiv}p(x,t) is a new potential variable which we introduced to make the prolonged system close completely, and it satisfies identically the compatibility conditions:

px=ψ1​ψ2,pt=−u​ψ1​ψ2−2​φ1​φ2.p_{x}=\psi_{1}\psi_{2},\ \ p_{t}=-u\psi_{1}\psi_{2}-2\varphi_{1}\varphi_{2}. (3.7)

Furthermore, the linearized equation of its symmetry σp\sigma^{p} read

σxp=ψ1​σψ2+ψ2​σψ1.\displaystyle\sigma^{p}_{x}=\psi_{1}\sigma^{\psi_{2}}+\psi_{2}\sigma^{\psi_{1}}. (3.8)

and a straightforward calculation shows that σp\sigma^{p} has the simple form

σp=p2.\displaystyle\sigma_{p}=p^{2}. (3.9)

Finally, the prolongation for nonlocal symmetry (3.1) is successfully localized by introducing variables {ψ1,ψ2,φ1,φ2,p}\{\psi_{1},\\ \psi_{2},\varphi_{1},\varphi_{2},p\} on the original variables {u,v}\{u,v\} with the equivalent vector expression

V\displaystyle V =\displaystyle= −2​(ψ1​φ2+ψ2​φ1)​∂∂u+(ψ1​φ2−ψ2​φ1)​∂∂v+p​ψ1​∂∂ψ1+p​ψ2​∂∂ψ2\displaystyle-2(\psi_{1}\varphi_{2}+\psi_{2}\varphi_{1})\frac{\partial}{\partial u}+(\psi_{1}\varphi_{2}-\psi_{2}\varphi_{1})\frac{\partial}{\partial v}+p\psi_{1}\frac{\partial}{\partial\psi_{1}}+p\psi_{2}\frac{\partial}{\partial\psi_{2}} (3.10)
+(ψ12​ψ2+p​φ1)​∂∂φ1+(ψ1​ψ22+p​φ2)​∂∂φ2+p2​∂∂p.\displaystyle+(\psi^{2}_{1}\psi_{2}+p\varphi_{1})\frac{\partial}{\partial\varphi_{1}}+(\psi_{1}\psi^{2}_{2}+p\varphi_{2})\frac{\partial}{\partial\varphi_{2}}+p^{2}\frac{\partial}{\partial p}.

Here, it is worthy to mention that if further consider the differential equation of the introduced variable pp from above localized procedure, one can find the corresponding differential equation is nothing but the Schwartz form of the HS-cKdV system (1.1)-(1.2)

3​ℋx3−6​ℋ​ℋx​ℋx​x+4​ℋ2​(2​𝒞t−(𝒞2)x−4​𝒞​𝒮x+ℋx​x​x−𝒞x​x​x)+16​ℋ3​𝒮x=0,\displaystyle 3\mathcal{H}^{3}_{x}-6\mathcal{H}\mathcal{H}_{x}\mathcal{H}_{xx}+4\mathcal{H}^{2}\Big(2\mathcal{C}_{t}-(\mathcal{C}^{2})_{x}-4\mathcal{C}\mathcal{S}_{x}+\mathcal{H}_{xxx}-\mathcal{C}_{xxx}\Big)+16\mathcal{H}^{3}\mathcal{S}_{x}=0, (3.11)

where ℋ=𝒮+2​𝒞\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{S}+2\mathcal{C}, 𝒮=px​x​xpx−3​px​x2px2\mathcal{S}=\frac{p_{xxx}}{p_{x}}-\frac{3p^{2}_{xx}}{p^{2}_{x}} and 𝒞=−ptpx\mathcal{C}=-\frac{p_{t}}{p_{x}} are all invariant under Möbious (conformal) transformation. The reason lies that the finite Möbious transformation

p→a+b​pc+d​p,(a​d≠b​c)p\rightarrow\frac{a+bp}{c+dp},\ \ (ad\neq bc)

possess its infinitesimal transformation p→p+ϵ​p2p\rightarrow p+\epsilon p^{2} in special case a=0,b=c=1a=0,b=c=1 and d=−ϵd=-\epsilon. The fact show us that the corresponding Schwartz form of a given differential equation derived usually by utilizing singularities analysis method can also be obtained through localization of the nonlocal symmetry from DT. Therefore, this method may provide a potential application to find Schwartz form of some integrable models, especially discrete integrable models which have some known DTs.

3.2 Finite symmetry transformation

For the related prolonged system from symmetry (3.1), it is natural to seek the finite transformation form of (3.10). By using Lie’s first theorem, we need to solve the following initial value problem

d​u^​(ϵ)d​ϵ=−2​ψ^1​φ^2−2​ψ^2​φ^1,d​v^​(ϵ)d​ϵ=ψ^1​φ^2−ψ^2​φ^1,d​ψ1^​(ϵ)d​ϵ=p^​ψ^1,d​ψ2^​(ϵ)d​ϵ=p^​ψ^2,\displaystyle\frac{d\hat{u}(\epsilon)}{d\epsilon}=-2\hat{\psi}_{1}\hat{\varphi}_{2}-2\hat{\psi}_{2}\hat{\varphi}_{1},\ \ \frac{d\hat{v}(\epsilon)}{d\epsilon}=\hat{\psi}_{1}\hat{\varphi}_{2}-\hat{\psi}_{2}\hat{\varphi}_{1},\ \ \frac{d\hat{\psi_{1}}(\epsilon)}{d\epsilon}=\hat{p}\hat{\psi}_{1},\frac{d\hat{\psi_{2}}(\epsilon)}{d\epsilon}=\hat{p}\hat{\psi}_{2},
d​φ1^​(ϵ)d​ϵ=ψ^12​ψ^2+p^​φ^1,d​ϕ2^​(ϵ)d​ϵ=ψ^1​ψ^22+p^​φ^2,d​p^​(ϵ)d​ϵ=p^2,\displaystyle\frac{d\hat{\varphi_{1}}(\epsilon)}{d\epsilon}=\hat{\psi}^{2}_{1}\hat{\psi}_{2}+\hat{p}\hat{\varphi}_{1},\ \ \frac{d\hat{\phi_{2}}(\epsilon)}{d\epsilon}=\hat{\psi}_{1}\hat{\psi}^{2}_{2}+\hat{p}\hat{\varphi}_{2},\ \ \frac{d\hat{p}(\epsilon)}{d\epsilon}=\hat{p}^{2}, (3.12)
u^​(0)=u,v^​(0)=v,ψ^1​(0)=ψ1,ψ^2​(0)=ψ2,φ^1​(0)=φ1,φ^2​(0)=φ2,p^​(0)=p,\displaystyle\hat{u}(0)=u,\ \ \hat{v}(0)=v,\ \ \hat{\psi}_{1}(0)=\psi_{1},\ \ \hat{\psi}_{2}(0)=\psi_{2},\ \ \hat{\varphi}_{1}(0)=\varphi_{1},\ \ \hat{\varphi}_{2}(0)=\varphi_{2},\ \ \hat{p}(0)=p,

where ϵ\epsilon is the group parameter.

By solving the initial value problem (3.12), we arrive at the symmetry group theorem as follow:

Theorem 1 If {u,v,ψ1,ψ2,φ1,φ2,p}\{u,v,\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\varphi_{1},\varphi_{2},p\} is the solution of the extended system consist of (1.1)-(2.4), (3.2) and (3.7)(\ref{hs-32}) with λ=0\lambda=0, so is {u^,v^,ψ^1,ψ^2,φ^1,φ^2,p^}\{\hat{u},\hat{v},\hat{\psi}_{1},\hat{\psi}_{2},\hat{\varphi}_{1},\hat{\varphi}_{2},\hat{p}\}

u^=u−2​ϵ​(ψ1​φ2+ψ2​φ1)1−ϵ​p−2​ϵ2​ψ12​ψ22(1−ϵ​p)2,\displaystyle\hat{u}=u-\frac{2\epsilon(\psi_{1}\varphi_{2}+\psi_{2}\varphi_{1})}{1-\epsilon p}-\frac{2\epsilon^{2}\psi^{2}_{1}\psi^{2}_{2}}{(1-\epsilon p)^{2}},
v^=v+ϵ⁡(ψ1​φ2+ψ2​φ1)1−ϵ​p+ϵ2​ψ12​ψ22(1−ϵ​p)2,\displaystyle\hat{v}=v+\frac{\epsilon(\psi_{1}\varphi_{2}+\psi_{2}\varphi_{1})}{1-\epsilon p}+\frac{\epsilon^{2}\psi^{2}_{1}\psi^{2}_{2}}{(1-\epsilon p)^{2}},
ψ^1=ψ11−ϵ​p,ψ^2=ψ21−ϵ​p,\displaystyle\hat{\psi}_{1}=\frac{\psi_{1}}{1-\epsilon p},\ \ \hat{\psi}_{2}=\frac{\psi_{2}}{1-\epsilon p}, (3.13)
φ^1=φ11−ϵ​p+ϵ​ψ2​ψ12(1−ϵ​p)2,φ^2=φ21−ϵ​p+ϵ​ψ1​ψ22(1−ϵ​p)2,\displaystyle\hat{\varphi}_{1}=\frac{\varphi_{1}}{1-\epsilon p}+\frac{\epsilon\psi_{2}\psi^{2}_{1}}{(1-\epsilon p)^{2}},\ \ \hat{\varphi}_{2}=\frac{\varphi_{2}}{1-\epsilon p}+\frac{\epsilon\psi_{1}\psi^{2}_{2}}{(1-\epsilon p)^{2}},
p^=p1−ϵ​p,\displaystyle\hat{p}=\frac{p}{1-\epsilon p},

with ϵ\epsilon is arbitrary group parameter.

For example, starting from the simple solution {u=λ122−λ222,v=λ222−λ122}\{u=\frac{\lambda^{2}_{1}}{2}-\frac{\lambda^{2}_{2}}{2},v=\frac{\lambda^{2}_{2}}{2}-\frac{\lambda^{2}_{1}}{2}\} of (1.1) and (1.2), we can derive the corresponding special solutions for the introduced dependent variables from (2.1)-(2.4), (3.2) and (3.7)(\ref{hs-32}) under the condition λ=0\lambda=0,

ψ1=cosh⁡(λ1​x+λ1​(λ12−3​λ22)2​t+ξ10),\displaystyle\psi_{1}=\cosh\Big(\lambda_{1}x+\frac{\lambda_{1}(\lambda^{2}_{1}-3\lambda^{2}_{2})}{2}t+\xi_{10}\Big),
ψ2=cosh⁡(λ2​x+λ2​(λ22−3​λ12)2​t+ξ20),\displaystyle\psi_{2}=\cosh\Big(\lambda_{2}x+\frac{\lambda_{2}(\lambda^{2}_{2}-3\lambda^{2}_{1})}{2}t+\xi_{20}\Big),
ϕ1=λ1​sinh⁡(λ1​x+λ1​(λ12−3​λ22)2​t+ξ10),\displaystyle\phi_{1}=\lambda_{1}\sinh\Big(\lambda_{1}x+\frac{\lambda_{1}(\lambda^{2}_{1}-3\lambda^{2}_{2})}{2}t+\xi_{10}\Big), (3.14)
ϕ2=λ2​sinh⁡(λ2​x+λ2​(λ22−3​λ12)2​t+ξ20),\displaystyle\phi_{2}=\lambda_{2}\sinh\Big(\lambda_{2}x+\frac{\lambda_{2}(\lambda^{2}_{2}-3\lambda^{2}_{1})}{2}t+\xi_{20}\Big),
p=sinh⁡ξ12​λ1−2​λ2+sinh⁡ξ22​λ1+2​λ2+ξ0.\displaystyle p=\frac{\sinh\xi_{1}}{2\lambda_{1}-2\lambda_{2}}+\frac{\sinh\xi_{2}}{2\lambda_{1}+2\lambda_{2}}+\xi_{0}.

Substituting (3.14) into (3.13) leads to the non-trivial solution of HS-cKdV system (1.1)-(1.2)

u=−λ122−λ222+ϵ[(λ1−λ2)sinhξ1+(λ1+λ2)sinhξ2]ϵ⁡(sinh⁡ξ12​λ1−2​λ2+sinh⁡ξ22​λ1+2​λ2+ξ0)−1−ϵ2​(cosh⁡ξ1+cosh⁡ξ2)216​[ϵ⁡(sinh⁡ξ12​λ1−2​λ2+sinh⁡ξ22​λ1+2​λ2+ξ0)−1]2,\displaystyle u=-\frac{\lambda^{2}_{1}}{2}-\frac{\lambda^{2}_{2}}{2}+\frac{\epsilon[(\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2})\sinh\xi_{1}+(\lambda_{1}+\lambda_{2})\sinh\xi_{2}]}{\epsilon(\frac{\sinh\xi_{1}}{2\lambda_{1}-2\lambda_{2}}+\frac{\sinh\xi_{2}}{2\lambda_{1}+2\lambda_{2}}+\xi_{0})-1}-\frac{\epsilon^{2}(\cosh\xi_{1}+\cosh\xi_{2})^{2}}{16[\epsilon(\frac{\sinh\xi_{1}}{2\lambda_{1}-2\lambda_{2}}+\frac{\sinh\xi_{2}}{2\lambda_{1}+2\lambda_{2}}+\xi_{0})-1]^{2}},
v=−λ122+λ222−ϵ[(λ1−λ2)sinhξ1+(λ1+λ2)sinhξ2]2​ϵ​(sinh⁡ξ12​λ1−2​λ2+sinh⁡ξ22​λ1+2​λ2+ξ0)−2+ϵ2​(cosh⁡ξ1+cosh⁡ξ2)232​[ϵ⁡(sinh⁡ξ12​λ1−2​λ2+sinh⁡ξ22​λ1+2​λ2+ξ0)−1]2,\displaystyle v=-\frac{\lambda^{2}_{1}}{2}+\frac{\lambda^{2}_{2}}{2}-\frac{\epsilon[(\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2})\sinh\xi_{1}+(\lambda_{1}+\lambda_{2})\sinh\xi_{2}]}{2\epsilon(\frac{\sinh\xi_{1}}{2\lambda_{1}-2\lambda_{2}}+\frac{\sinh\xi_{2}}{2\lambda_{1}+2\lambda_{2}}+\xi_{0})-2}+\frac{\epsilon^{2}(\cosh\xi_{1}+\cosh\xi_{2})^{2}}{32[\epsilon(\frac{\sinh\xi_{1}}{2\lambda_{1}-2\lambda_{2}}+\frac{\sinh\xi_{2}}{2\lambda_{1}+2\lambda_{2}}+\xi_{0})-1]^{2}}, (3.15)

with

ξ1=(λ1−λ2)​[x+λ12+4​λ1​λ2+λ222​t]+ξ10−ξ20,\displaystyle\xi_{1}=(\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2})[x+\frac{\lambda^{2}_{1}+4\lambda_{1}\lambda_{2}+\lambda^{2}_{2}}{2}t]+\xi_{10}-\xi_{20},
ξ2=(λ1+λ2)​[x+λ12−4​λ1​λ2+λ222​t]+ξ10+ξ20,\displaystyle\xi_{2}=(\lambda_{1}+\lambda_{2})[x+\frac{\lambda^{2}_{1}-4\lambda_{1}\lambda_{2}+\lambda^{2}_{2}}{2}t]+\xi_{10}+\xi_{20},

where ξ0,ξ10\xi_{0},\xi_{10} and ξ20\xi_{20} are arbitrary constants.

It is necessary to point out that the finite transformation exhibited in Theorem 1 is distinct from the original DT in above section. Indeed, it is equivalent to the so-called Levi transformation, or the second type of Darboux transformations. At the algebra level, two different types of finite transformation possesses the same infinitesimal expression (3.1). Besides, the last equation of (3.13) is nothing but the corresponding Möbious transformation in the front analysis about Schwartz form (3.11) of the original system.

3.3 Similarity reductions of the prolonged system

In this section, our main aim is to seek for some exact solutions from the prolonged system to construct some novel solutions of original HS-cKdV system. Therefore, we employ the classical Lie symmetry method to search for similarity reductions of the whole prolonged system.

Accordingly, we consider the one-parameter group of infinitesimal transformations in {x,t,u\{x,t,u,vv,ψ1\psi_{1},
ψ2\psi_{2},φ1\varphi_{1},φ2\varphi_{2},p}p\} given by

{x,t,u,v,ψ1,ψ2,φ1,φ2,p}→{x+ϵ​X,t+ϵ​T,u+ϵ​U,v+ϵ​V,ψ1+ϵ​ψ1,ψ2+ϵ​Ψ2,φ1+ϵ​Φ1,φ2+ϵ​Φ2,p+ϵ​P}\displaystyle\{x,t,u,v,\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\varphi_{1},\varphi_{2},p\}{\rightarrow}\{x{+}\epsilon X,t{+}\epsilon T,u{+}\epsilon U,v{+}\epsilon V,\psi_{1}{+}\epsilon\psi_{1},\psi_{2}{+}\epsilon\Psi_{2},\varphi_{1}{+}\epsilon\Phi_{1},\varphi_{2}{+}\epsilon\Phi_{2},p{+}\epsilon P\}

with

σu=X​ux+T​ut−U,σv=X​vx+T​vt−V,\displaystyle\sigma^{u}=Xu_{x}+Tu_{t}-U,\ \ \sigma^{v}=Xv_{x}+Tv_{t}-V,
σψ1=X​ψ1​x+T​ψ1​t−Ψ1,σψ2=X​ψ2​x+T​ψ2​t−Ψ2,\displaystyle\sigma^{\psi_{1}}=X\psi_{1x}+T\psi_{1t}-\Psi_{1},\ \ \sigma^{\psi_{2}}=X\psi_{2x}+T\psi_{2t}-\Psi_{2},

σp=X​px+T​pt−P,\displaystyle\sigma^{p}=Xp_{x}+Tp_{t}-P,

where X,T,U,V,Ψ1,Ψ2,Φ1,Φ2X,T,U,V,\Psi_{1},\Psi_{2},\Phi_{1},\Phi_{2} and PP are functions with respect to {x,t,u,v,ψ1,ψ2,φ1,φ2,p}\{x,t,u,v,\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\varphi_{1},\varphi_{2},p\}, and ϵ\epsilon is a small parameter. Substituting (3.16) into the symmetry equations, i.e., the linearized equations of the prolonged system obtained in above section

σtu−12​σx​x​xu−3​u​σxu−3​σu​ux+6​v​σxv+6​σv​vx=0,σtv+σx​x​xv+3​σu​vx+3​u​σxv=0\displaystyle\sigma^{u}_{t}-\frac{1}{2}\sigma^{u}_{xxx}-3u\sigma^{u}_{x}-3\sigma^{u}u_{x}+6v\sigma^{v}_{x}+6\sigma^{v}v_{x}=0,\ \ \sigma^{v}_{t}+\sigma^{v}_{xxx}+3\sigma^{u}v_{x}+3u\sigma^{v}_{x}=0

σtψ1+12​σψ1​(ux−2​vx)+12​ψ1​(σxu−2​σxv)−(u−2​v)​σxψ1−(σu−2​σv)​ψ1​x=0,\displaystyle\sigma^{\psi_{1}}_{t}+\frac{1}{2}\sigma^{\psi_{1}}(u_{x}-2v_{x})+\frac{1}{2}\psi_{1}(\sigma^{u}_{x}-2\sigma^{v}_{x})-(u-2v)\sigma^{\psi_{1}}_{x}-(\sigma^{u}-2\sigma^{v})\psi_{1x}=0,

σxψ1−σφ1=0,σxψ2−σφ2=0,\displaystyle\sigma^{\psi_{1}}_{x}-\sigma^{\varphi_{1}}=0,\ \ \sigma^{\psi_{2}}_{x}-\sigma^{\varphi_{2}}=0,

X=c1​x+c4,T=3​c1​t+c2,\displaystyle X=c_{1}x+c_{4},\ \ T=3c_{1}t+c_{2},
U=−2​c1​u−2​c3​(ψ1​φ2+ψ2​φ1),V=−2​c1​v+c3​(ψ1​ϕ2−ψ2​ϕ1),\displaystyle U=-2c_{1}u-2c_{3}(\psi_{1}\varphi_{2}+\psi_{2}\varphi_{1}),\ \ V=-2c_{1}v+c_{3}(\psi_{1}\phi_{2}-\psi_{2}\phi_{1}),

where cic_{i} (i=1​…​7)(i{=}1...7) are arbitrary constants. To give some corresponding group invariant solutions, we need to solve the following characteristic equations:

From the expression of the last exact solution (3.30), we know that it potentially reflects the interaction between the soliton and the cnoidal periodic wave. As Shin has mentioned [26, 27, 28], these soliton++cnoidal wave solutions can be easily applicable to the analysis of physically interesting processes.

The dynamics behavior of the soliton++cnoidal wave solution given by (3.30) at two different choices of the parameters b0,hb_{0},h and mm are illustrated in Fig.1 and 2. In Fig. 1, when m≠1m{\neq}1, we can see that the component uu exhibits a bell-shaped bright soliton propagates on a cnoidal wave background, whereas, periodic wave in the component vv occurs at the corner of a kink-shaped soliton. When m=1m{=}1, the Jacobian elliptic periodic functions in (3.30) reduces to the general hyperbolic functions, so the characteristics of the two-soltion is depicted distinctly in Fig. 2.

Q1​z2​(z)=a1​Q1​(z)+a2​Q12​(z)+a3​Q13​(z)+4​Q14​(z)Q^{2}_{1z}(z)=a_{1}Q_{1}(z)+a_{2}Q^{2}_{1}(z)+a_{3}Q^{3}_{1}(z)+4Q^{4}_{1}(z) (3.33)

with a1=c6−c5a_{1}=c_{6}-c_{5} and a2=4​c4a_{2}=4c_{4}.

Hence, in this subcase, from Eq.(3.33), the final exact solutions consisted of Jacobian elliptic periodic function and rational function denote the interactions among cnoidal periodic waves and rational waves for the HS-cKdV system.

4 Integrable models from nonlocal symmetry

4.1 Negative HS-cKdV hierarchy

As we known, the existence of infinitely many symmetry naturally leads to the existence of integrable hierarchies. For the general hierarchies, one can obtain them form a trivial symmetry of the original integrable system using recursion operator. For example, considering the corresponding recursion operator [29, 30, 31], the HS-cKdV system has the following high order symmetry

uτ\displaystyle u_{\tau} =\displaystyle= (12​u4​x+5​u​ux2−5​v​vx​x+52​ux2−8​u​v2+5​u3)x−v2​ux,\displaystyle(\frac{1}{2}u_{4x}+5uu^{2}_{x}-5vv_{xx}+\frac{5}{2}u^{2}_{x}-8uv^{2}+5u^{3})_{x}-v^{2}u_{x}, (4.1)
vτ\displaystyle v_{\tau} =\displaystyle= (−v4​x−2​ux​vx−6​u​vx​x−53​v3)x−3​ux​x​vx−5​u2​vx.\displaystyle(-v_{4x}-2u_{x}v_{x}-6uv_{xx}-\frac{5}{3}v^{3})_{x}-3u_{xx}v_{x}-5u^{2}v_{x}. (4.2)

It is remarkable that the reduction v=0v=0 in this symmetry gives us the Lax equation [49].

Recently, Lou [14, 15, 16, 17] has extended some (1+1)-dimensional integrable model to some corresponding negative hierarchy through a set of nonlocal infinitely many symmetries which can be obtained from the kernels of a reversible recursion operator. However, to obtain the inverse of the known recursion operator is still a difficult work, especially for the high dimensional system and the high order operator. Here, to obtain the negative HS-cKdV hierarchy, we would like to employ one kind of method without the recursion operator [10].

Starting from the nonlocal symmetry from DT given by (2.23), we let

K0u​(λ)≡−2​(ψ1​ψ2)x,K0v​(λ)≡ψ1​ψ2​x−ψ2​ψ1​x,K^{u}_{0}(\lambda)\equiv-2(\psi_{1}\psi_{2})_{x},\ \ K^{v}_{0}(\lambda)\equiv\psi_{1}\psi_{2x}-\psi_{2}\psi_{1x}, (4.3)

where ψ1\psi_{1} and ψ2\psi_{2} are determined by Lax pair (2.1)-(2.4) with λ≠0\lambda\neq 0. Because of the parameter λ\lambda being an arbitrary constant, we can treat it as a small parameter and expand K0u​(λ)K^{u}_{0}(\lambda) and K0v​(λ)K^{v}_{0}(\lambda) as a series in λ\lambda:

K0u​(λ)=∑n=0∞1n!​∂n∂λn​K0u​(λ)|λ=0​λn,K0v​(λ)=∑n=0∞1n!​∂n∂λn​K0v​(λ)|λ=0​λn,K^{u}_{0}(\lambda)=\sum^{\infty}_{n=0}\frac{1}{n!}\frac{\partial^{n}}{\partial\lambda^{n}}K^{u}_{0}(\lambda)\bigg|_{\lambda=0}\lambda^{n},\ \ K^{v}_{0}(\lambda)=\sum^{\infty}_{n=0}\frac{1}{n!}\frac{\partial^{n}}{\partial\lambda^{n}}K^{v}_{0}(\lambda)\bigg|_{\lambda=0}\lambda^{n}, (4.4)

Substituting equation (4.4) into the corresponding symmetry definition equation of the HS-cKdV system (1.1)-(1.2), we can conclude that

Knu​(λ)=1n!​∂n∂λn​K0u​(λ)|λ=0​λn,Knv​(λ)=1n!​∂n∂λn​K0v​(λ)|λ=0​λn,K^{u}_{n}(\lambda)=\frac{1}{n!}\frac{\partial^{n}}{\partial\lambda^{n}}K^{u}_{0}(\lambda)\bigg|_{\lambda=0}\lambda^{n},\ \ K^{v}_{n}(\lambda)=\frac{1}{n!}\frac{\partial^{n}}{\partial\lambda^{n}}K^{v}_{0}(\lambda)\bigg|_{\lambda=0}\lambda^{n}, (4.5)

must also be a symmetry of the HS-cKdV system for all nn (n=0,1,2​…)(n=0,1,2...). At the same time, we let ψ1=ψ1​(λ)\psi_{1}=\psi_{1}(\lambda) and ψ2=ψ2​(λ)\psi_{2}=\psi_{2}(\lambda) have the formal series form

ψ1=∑k=0∞ψ1​[k]​λk,ψ2=∑k=0∞ψ2​[k]​λk,\psi_{1}=\sum^{\infty}_{k=0}\psi_{1}[k]\lambda^{k},\ \ \psi_{2}=\sum^{\infty}_{k=0}\psi_{2}[k]\lambda^{k}, (4.6)

where ψ1​[k]\psi_{1}[k] and ψ2​[k]\psi_{2}[k] are λ\lambda independent and should be determined later.

Substituting (4.5) and (4.6) into (2.1) and (2.2), and collecting the coefficients of λ\lambda yields

(∂2+u+v)ψ1[0]=0,(∂2+u+v)ψ1[k]=−ψ2[k−1],\displaystyle(\partial^{2}+u+v)\psi_{1}[0]=0,\ \ (\partial^{2}+u+v)\psi_{1}[k]=-\psi_{2}[k-1], (4.7)
(∂2+u−v)ψ2[0]=0,(∂2+u−v)ψ2[k]=ψ1[k−1].\displaystyle(\partial^{2}+u-v)\psi_{2}[0]=0,\ \ (\partial^{2}+u-v)\psi_{2}[k]=\psi_{1}[k-1]. (4.8)

Then, ψ1​[k]\psi_{1}[k] and ψ2​[k]\psi_{2}[k] can be solved recursively as

ψ1[k]=L1−1ψ2[k−1]=L1−1L2−1ψ1[k−2]⋯={(L2​L1)−k2​ψ1​[0],kis even(L2​L1)−k−12​L1−1​ψ2​[0],kis odd\displaystyle\psi_{1}[k]=L_{1}^{-1}\psi_{2}[k{-}1]=L_{1}^{-1}L_{2}^{-1}\psi_{1}[k{-}2]\cdots=\begin{cases}(L_{2}L_{1})^{-\frac{k}{2}}\psi_{1}[0],\ \ k\ \ \mbox{is even}\\ (L_{2}L_{1})^{{-}\frac{k{-}1}{2}}L^{-1}_{1}\psi_{2}[0],\ \ k\ \ \mbox{is odd}\end{cases} (4.9)
ψ2[k]=L2−1ψ1[k−1]=L2−1L1−1ψ2[k−2]⋯={(L1​L2)−k2​ψ2​[0],kis even(L1​L2)−k−12​L2−1​ψ1​[0],kis odd\displaystyle\psi_{2}[k]=L_{2}^{-1}\psi_{1}[k{-}1]=L_{2}^{-1}L_{1}^{-1}\psi_{2}[k{-}2]\cdots=\begin{cases}(L_{1}L_{2})^{-\frac{k}{2}}\psi_{2}[0],\ \ k\ \ \mbox{is even}\\ (L_{1}L_{2})^{{-}\frac{k{-}1}{2}}L^{-1}_{2}\psi_{1}[0],\ \ k\ \ \mbox{is odd}\end{cases} (4.10)
L1=−∂2−u−v,L2=∂2+u−v,\displaystyle L_{1}=-\partial^{2}-u-v,\ \ L_{2}=\partial^{2}+u-v,

which leads (4.6) to

ψ1=∑k1=0,2,4⋯∞(L2L1)−k12ψ1[0]λk1+∑k2=1,3,5⋯∞(L2L1)−k2−12L1−1ψ2[0]λk2,\displaystyle\psi_{1}=\sum^{\infty}_{k_{1}=0,2,4\cdots}(L_{2}L_{1})^{-\frac{k_{1}}{2}}\psi_{1}[0]\lambda^{k_{1}}+\sum^{\infty}_{k_{2}=1,3,5\cdots}(L_{2}L_{1})^{{-}\frac{k_{2}{-}1}{2}}L^{-1}_{1}\psi_{2}[0]\lambda^{k_{2}}, (4.11)
ψ2=∑k3=0,2,4⋯∞(L1L2)−k32ψ2[0]λk3+∑k4=1,3,5⋯∞(L1L2)−k4−12L2−1ψ1[0]λk4.\displaystyle\psi_{2}=\sum^{\infty}_{k_{3}=0,2,4\cdots}(L_{1}L_{2})^{-\frac{k_{3}}{2}}\psi_{2}[0]\lambda^{k_{3}}+\sum^{\infty}_{k_{4}=1,3,5\cdots}(L_{1}L_{2})^{{-}\frac{k_{4}{-}1}{2}}L^{-1}_{2}\psi_{1}[0]\lambda^{k_{4}}. (4.12)

Finally, the set of the nonlocal symmetries can be obtained by substituting (4.11) and (4.12) into (4.5):

{Kun=−2∑nk1=0,2,4⋯(Ξ1Ξ3)x−2∑n−1k2=1,3,5⋯(Ξ2Ξ4)x,Kvn=∑nk1=0,2,4⋯(Ξ1Ξ3​x−Ξ3Ξ1​x)+∑n−1k2=1,3,5⋯(Ξ2Ξ4​x−Ξ4Ξ2​x),​nis even,\displaystyle\begin{cases}K^{u}_{n}=-2\sum^{n}_{k_{1}=0,2,4\cdots}(\Xi_{1}\Xi_{3})_{x}-2\sum^{n-1}_{k_{2}=1,3,5\cdots}(\Xi_{2}\Xi_{4})_{x},\\ K^{v}_{n}=\sum^{n}_{k_{1}=0,2,4\cdots}(\Xi_{1}\Xi_{3x}-\Xi_{3}\Xi_{1x})+\sum^{n-1}_{k_{2}=1,3,5\cdots}(\Xi_{2}\Xi_{4x}-\Xi_{4}\Xi_{2x}),\end{cases}n\ \ \mbox{is even}, (4.13)
{Kun=−2∑n−1k1=0,2,4⋯(Ξ1Ξ6)x−2∑nk2=1,3,5⋯(Ξ2Ξ5)x,Kvn=∑n−1k1=0,2,4⋯(Ξ1Ξ6​x−Ξ6Ξ1​x)+∑nk2=1,3,5⋯(Ξ2Ξ5​x−Ξ5Ξ2​x),​nis odd,\displaystyle\begin{cases}K^{u}_{n}=-2\sum^{n-1}_{k_{1}=0,2,4\cdots}(\Xi_{1}\Xi_{6})_{x}-2\sum^{n}_{k_{2}=1,3,5\cdots}(\Xi_{2}\Xi_{5})_{x},\\ K^{v}_{n}=\sum^{n-1}_{k_{1}=0,2,4\cdots}(\Xi_{1}\Xi_{6x}-\Xi_{6}\Xi_{1x})+\sum^{n}_{k_{2}=1,3,5\cdots}(\Xi_{2}\Xi_{5x}-\Xi_{5}\Xi_{2x}),\end{cases}n\ \ \mbox{is odd}, (4.14)

where

Ξ1=(L2​L1)−k12​ψ1​[0],Ξ2=(L2​L1)−k2−12​L1−1​ψ2​[0],\displaystyle\Xi_{1}=(L_{2}L_{1})^{-\frac{k_{1}}{2}}\psi_{1}[0],\ \ \ \ \Xi_{2}=(L_{2}L_{1})^{{-}\frac{k_{2}{-}1}{2}}L^{-1}_{1}\psi_{2}[0],
Ξ3=(L1​L2)−n−k12​ψ2​[0],Ξ4=(L1​L2)−n−k2−12​L2−1​ψ1​[0],\displaystyle\Xi_{3}=(L_{1}L_{2})^{-\frac{n-k_{1}}{2}}\psi_{2}[0],\ \ \Xi_{4}=(L_{1}L_{2})^{{-}\frac{n-k_{2}{-}1}{2}}L^{-1}_{2}\psi_{1}[0],
Ξ5=(L1​L2)−n−k22​ψ2​[0],Ξ6=(L1​L2)−n−k1−12​L2−1​ψ1​[0].\displaystyle\Xi_{5}=(L_{1}L_{2})^{-\frac{n-k_{2}}{2}}\psi_{2}[0],\ \ \Xi_{6}=(L_{1}L_{2})^{{-}\frac{n-k_{1}{-}1}{2}}L^{-1}_{2}\psi_{1}[0].

From the set of the nonlocal symmetries, the negative HS-cKdV hierarchy (the flow equations of the HS-cKdV equation corresponding to the nonlocal symmetries) follows immediately:

{ut=Kun,vt=Kvn,L1ψ1[0]=0,L2ψ2[0]=0,\displaystyle\begin{cases}u_{t}=K^{u}_{n},\ \ v_{t}=K^{v}_{n},\\ L_{1}\psi_{1}[0]=0,\ \ L_{2}\psi_{2}[0]=0,\end{cases} (4.15)

where KnuK^{u}_{n} and KnvK^{v}_{n} are expressed by (4.13) and (4.14).

Using the Miura transformation [47, 48]

u=−12​Fx​x−14​Fx2−14​Gx2,v=−12​Gx​x−12​Fx​Gx,\displaystyle u=-\frac{1}{2}F_{xx}-\frac{1}{4}F^{2}_{x}-\frac{1}{4}G^{2}_{x},\ \ v=-\frac{1}{2}G_{xx}-\frac{1}{2}F_{x}G_{x}, (4.16)

the first one of negative HS-cKdV hierarchy (4.15) is transformed to a coupled sinh-Gordon equations:

Fx​t=sinh⁡(F)+f,Gx​t=sinh⁡(F)+g,\displaystyle F_{xt}=\sinh(F)+f,\ \ G_{xt}=\sinh(F)+g,
[(4​s−1)​exp⁡(F)−f]​Fx+[12​sinh⁡(F)−g]​Gx−fx=0,\displaystyle[(4s-1)\exp(F)-f]F_{x}+[\frac{1}{2}\sinh(F)-g]G_{x}-f_{x}=0, (4.17)
[f−g−2​s​exp⁡(F)]​(Fx−Gx)+fx−gx−2​s​exp⁡(F)​Fx=0.\displaystyle[f-g-2s\exp(F)](F_{x}-G_{x})+f_{x}-g_{x}-2s\exp(F)F_{x}=0.

with ss is an arbitrary constant. When s=14s=\frac{1}{4} and G=0G=0, (4.17) is just the usual sinh-Gordon equation.

Further, the complicated integrodifferential hierarchy (4.15) can be written as a simple equivalent differential equation system ((L2​L1)m+1​Pm=ψ1​[0],(L1​L2)m​L1​Qm=ψ2​[0])((L_{2}L_{1})^{m+1}P_{m}=\psi_{1}[0],(L_{1}L_{2})^{m}L_{1}Q_{m}=\psi_{2}[0])

{ut=−2∑mj1=0(Ξ1Ξ3)x−2∑m−1j2=0(Ξ2Ξ4)x,vt=∑j1=0m(Ξ1​Ξ3​x−Ξ3​Ξ1​x)+∑j2=0m−1(Ξ2​Ξ4​x−Ξ4​Ξ2​x),​n=2​mis even,\displaystyle\begin{cases}u_{t}=-2\sum^{m}_{j_{1}=0}(\Xi_{1}\Xi_{3})_{x}-2\sum^{m-1}_{j_{2}=0}(\Xi_{2}\Xi_{4})_{x},\\ v_{t}=\sum^{m}_{j_{1}=0}(\Xi_{1}\Xi_{3x}-\Xi_{3}\Xi_{1x})+\sum^{m-1}_{j_{2}=0}(\Xi_{2}\Xi_{4x}-\Xi_{4}\Xi_{2x}),\end{cases}n=2m\ \ \mbox{is even}, (4.18)
{ut=−2∑mj1=0(Ξ1Ξ6)x−2∑mj2=0(Ξ2Ξ5)x,vt=∑j1=0m(Ξ1​Ξ6​x−Ξ6​Ξ1​x)+∑j2=0m(Ξ2​Ξ5​x−Ξ5​Ξ2​x),​n=2​m+1is odd,\displaystyle\begin{cases}u_{t}=-2\sum^{m}_{j_{1}=0}(\Xi_{1}\Xi_{6})_{x}-2\sum^{m}_{j_{2}=0}(\Xi_{2}\Xi_{5})_{x},\\ v_{t}=\sum^{m}_{j_{1}=0}(\Xi_{1}\Xi_{6x}-\Xi_{6}\Xi_{1x})+\sum^{m}_{j_{2}=0}(\Xi_{2}\Xi_{5x}-\Xi_{5}\Xi_{2x}),\end{cases}n=2m+1\ \ \mbox{is odd}, (4.19)
L1​(L2​L1)m+1​Pm=0,L2​(L1​L2)m​L1​Qm=0,\displaystyle L_{1}(L_{2}L_{1})^{m+1}P_{m}=0,L_{2}(L_{1}L_{2})^{m}L_{1}Q_{m}=0, (4.20)

with

Ξ1=(L2​L1)m−j1+1​Pm,Ξ2=(L2​L1)m−j2​Qm,\displaystyle\Xi_{1}=(L_{2}L_{1})^{m-j_{1}+1}P_{m},\ \ \Xi_{2}=(L_{2}L_{1})^{m-j_{2}}Q_{m},
Ξ3=(L1​L2)j1​L1​Qm,Ξ4=(L1​L2)j2+1​L1​Pm,\displaystyle\Xi_{3}=(L_{1}L_{2})^{j_{1}}L_{1}Q_{m},\ \ \Xi_{4}=(L_{1}L_{2})^{j_{2}+1}L_{1}P_{m},
Ξ5=(L1​L2)j2​L1​Qm,Ξ6=(L1​L2)j1​L1​Pm.\displaystyle\Xi_{5}=(L_{1}L_{2})^{j_{2}}L_{1}Q_{m},\ \ \Xi_{6}=(L_{1}L_{2})^{j_{1}}L_{1}P_{m}.

In ref.[18], only the first negative HS-cKdV system is given. Now we provide the whole negative HS-cKdV hierarchy by simple differential form.

4.2 Lower-dimensional and Higher-dimensional integrable systems

From the nonlocal symmetry of the HS-cKdV system and Proposition 5 in Section 2, a nontrivial nonlocal symmetry related to the spectral functions ψ1\psi_{1} and ψ2\psi_{2} can be obtained,

σN=(σNu,σNv)≡(−∑i=1N2ai(ψ1​iψ2​i)x,∑i=1Nai(ψ1​iψ2​i​x−ψ2​iψ1​i​x))\displaystyle\sigma_{N}=(\sigma^{u}_{N},\sigma^{v}_{N})\equiv\Big(-\sum^{N}_{i=1}2a_{i}(\psi_{1i}\psi_{2i})_{x},\sum^{N}_{i=1}a_{i}(\psi_{1i}\psi_{2ix}-\psi_{2i}\psi_{1ix})\Big) (4.21)

where aia_{i} are constants, i=1,2,…,Ni=1,2,...,N, and {ψ1​i,ψ2​i}\{\psi_{1i},\psi_{2i}\} are independent solutions of the Lax pair (2.1)-(2.4) with λ=0\lambda=0.

A. Lower-dimensional integrable systems

Usually, every one symmetry of a higher dimensional model can lead the original one to its lower form. Now, considering

ux=−∑i=1N2ai(ψ1​iψ2​i)x,vx=∑i=1Nai(ψ1​iψ2​i​x−ψ2​iψ1​i​x),u_{x}=-\sum^{N}_{i=1}2a_{i}(\psi_{1i}\psi_{2i})_{x},\ \ v_{x}=\sum^{N}_{i=1}a_{i}(\psi_{1i}\psi_{2ix}-\psi_{2i}\psi_{1ix}), (4.22)

as a symmetry constraint condition and acting it on the xx-part of the Lax pair (2.1)-(2.2) for ψ1=ψ1​i\psi_{1}=\psi_{1i} and ψ2=ψ2​i\psi_{2}=\psi_{2i}, we have the lower dimensional 2N-component differential system

ψ1​i​ψ1​i​x​x​x−ψ1​i​x​ψ1​i​x​x−∑n=1Nan​(ψ1​n​ψ2​n​x+3​ψ2​n​ψ1​n​x)​ψ1​i2=0,\displaystyle\psi_{1i}\psi_{1ixxx}-\psi_{1ix}\psi_{1ixx}-\sum^{N}_{n=1}a_{n}(\psi_{1n}\psi_{2nx}+3\psi_{2n}\psi_{1nx})\psi^{2}_{1i}=0,
ψ2​i​ψ2​i​x​x​x−ψ2​i​x​ψ2​i​x​x−∑n=1Nan​(ψ2​n​ψ1​n​x+3​ψ1​n​ψ2​n​x)​ψ2​i2=0.\displaystyle\psi_{2i}\psi_{2ixxx}-\psi_{2ix}\psi_{2ixx}-\sum^{N}_{n=1}a_{n}(\psi_{2n}\psi_{1nx}+3\psi_{1n}\psi_{2nx})\psi^{2}_{2i}=0. (4.23)

When N=1N=1, ψ10=ψ1,ψ20=ψ2\psi_{10}=\psi_{1},\psi_{20}=\psi_{2}, system (4.23) is the differential equations

ψ1​ψ1​x​x​x−ψ1​x​ψ1​x​x−3​a1​ψ12​ψ2​ψ1​x−a1​ψ13​ψ2​x=0,\displaystyle\psi_{1}\psi_{1xxx}-\psi_{1x}\psi_{1xx}-3a_{1}\psi^{2}_{1}\psi_{2}\psi_{1x}-a_{1}\psi^{3}_{1}\psi_{2x}=0,
ψ2​ψ2​x​x​x−ψ2​x​ψ2​x​x−3​a1​ψ22​ψ1​ψ2​x−a1​ψ23​ψ1​x=0,\displaystyle\psi_{2}\psi_{2xxx}-\psi_{2x}\psi_{2xx}-3a_{1}\psi^{2}_{2}\psi_{1}\psi_{2x}-a_{1}\psi^{3}_{2}\psi_{1x}=0, (4.24)

More especially, under the condition ψ1=ψ2\psi_{1}=\psi_{2}, system (4.24) becomes the elliptic equation

ψ1​x2=b0+b1​ψ12+a1​ψ14,\displaystyle\psi^{2}_{1x}=b_{0}+b_{1}\psi^{2}_{1}+a_{1}\psi^{4}_{1},

where b0b_{0} and b1b_{1} are arbitrary constants. So we call system (4.24) a coupled elliptic equation.

Substituting (4.22) into (2.3) and (2.4) and using (4.23), the tt-part of the Lax pair becomes the generalized 2N-component coupled modified KdV (mKdV) system

ψ1​i​t=−ψ1​i​x​x​x+3​∑n=1Nan​(ψ1​n​ψ2​n)x​ψ1​i−3​∑n=1Nan​∂x−1(ψ1​n​ψ2​n​x−ψ2​n​ψ1​n​x)​ψ1​i​x,\displaystyle\hskip-28.45274pt\psi_{1it}=-\psi_{1ixxx}+3\sum^{N}_{n=1}a_{n}(\psi_{1n}\psi_{2n})_{x}\psi_{1i}-3\sum^{N}_{n=1}a_{n}\partial^{-1}_{x}(\psi_{1n}\psi_{2nx}-\psi_{2n}\psi_{1nx})\psi_{1ix},
ψ2​i​t=−ψ2​i​x​x​x+3​∑n=1Nan​(ψ1​n​ψ2​n)x​ψ2​i+3​∑n=1Nan​∂x−1(ψ1​n​ψ2​n​x−ψ2​n​ψ1​n​x)​ψ2​i​x.\displaystyle\hskip-28.45274pt\psi_{2it}=-\psi_{2ixxx}+3\sum^{N}_{n=1}a_{n}(\psi_{1n}\psi_{2n})_{x}\psi_{2i}+3\sum^{N}_{n=1}a_{n}\partial^{-1}_{x}(\psi_{1n}\psi_{2nx}-\psi_{2n}\psi_{1nx})\psi_{2ix}. (4.25)

When N=1,a1=1N=1,a_{1}=1, ψ10=ψ1,ψ20=ψ2\psi_{10}=\psi_{1},\psi_{20}=\psi_{2}, system (4.25) is the generalized coupled mKdV equations,

ψ1​t=−ψ1​x​x​x+3​ψ1​(ψ1​ψ2)x−3​v​ψ1​x,\displaystyle\psi_{1t}=-\psi_{1xxx}+3\psi_{1}(\psi_{1}\psi_{2})_{x}-3v\psi_{1x},
ψ2​t=−ψ2​x​x​x+3​ψ2​(ψ1​ψ2)x+3​v​ψ2​x,\displaystyle\psi_{2t}=-\psi_{2xxx}+3\psi_{2}(\psi_{1}\psi_{2})_{x}+3v\psi_{2x}, (4.26)
vx=ψ1​ψ2​x−ψ2​ψ1​x.\displaystyle v_{x}=\psi_{1}\psi_{2x}-\psi_{2}\psi_{1x}.

B. Higher-dimensional integrable systems

To obtain some higher dimensional integrable models, one may introduce some internal parameters. It is obvious that system (1.1)-(1.2) are invariant under the internal parameter translation, say yy translation. That is to say (uy,vy)(u_{y},v_{y}) is also a symmetry of the HS-cKdV system. So we can use

uy=−∑i=1N2ai(ψ1​iψ2​i)x,vy=∑i=1Nai(ψ1​iψ2​i​x−ψ2​iψ1​i​x),\displaystyle u_{y}=-\sum^{N}_{i=1}2a_{i}(\psi_{1i}\psi_{2i})_{x},\ \ v_{y}=\sum^{N}_{i=1}a_{i}(\psi_{1i}\psi_{2ix}-\psi_{2i}\psi_{1ix}), (4.27)

as a generalized symmetry constraint condition.

Substituting (4.27) into the xx-part of the Lax pair (2.1)-(2.2) for ψ1=ψ1​i\psi_{1}=\psi_{1i} and ψ2=ψ2​i\psi_{2}=\psi_{2i} yields a higher dimensional 2N-component differential system

ψ1​i​x​x−ψ1​i​∑n=1Nan​∂y−1(ψ1​n​ψ2​n​x+3​ψ2​n​ψ1​n​x)=0,\displaystyle\psi_{1ixx}-\psi_{1i}\sum^{N}_{n=1}a_{n}\partial^{-1}_{y}(\psi_{1n}\psi_{2nx}+3\psi_{2n}\psi_{1nx})=0,
ψ2​i​x​x−ψ2​i​∑n=1Nan​∂y−1(ψ2​n​ψ1​n​x+3​ψ1​n​ψ2​n​x)=0.\displaystyle\psi_{2ixx}-\psi_{2i}\sum^{N}_{n=1}a_{n}\partial^{-1}_{y}(\psi_{2n}\psi_{1nx}+3\psi_{1n}\psi_{2nx})=0. (4.28)

When we take N=1N=1, a1=1a_{1}=1, ψ10=ψ1,ψ20=ψ2\psi_{10}=\psi_{1},\psi_{20}=\psi_{2}, and use the same Miura transformation (4.16), the system (4.28) also reduces to the same coupled sinh-Gordon equations with Eqs. (4.17).

Considering (4.27) and the xx-part of the Lax pair (2.1)-(2.2) for ψ1=ψ1​i\psi_{1}=\psi_{1i} and ψ2=ψ2​i\psi_{2}=\psi_{2i} produces a higher dimensional 2N-component differential system

ψ1​i​t=−ψ1​i​x​x​x+3​∑n=1Nan​∂y−1(ψ1​n​ψ2​n)x​x​ψ1​i−3​∑n=1Nan​∂y−1(ψ1​n​ψ2​n​x−ψ2​n​ψ1​n​x)​ψ1​i​x,\displaystyle\hskip-42.67912pt\psi_{1it}=-\psi_{1ixxx}+3\sum^{N}_{n=1}a_{n}\partial^{-1}_{y}(\psi_{1n}\psi_{2n})_{xx}\psi_{1i}-3\sum^{N}_{n=1}a_{n}\partial^{-1}_{y}(\psi_{1n}\psi_{2nx}-\psi_{2n}\psi_{1nx})\psi_{1ix},
ψ2​i​t=−ψ2​i​x​x​x+3​∑n=1Nan​∂y−1(ψ1​n​ψ2​n)x​x​ψ2​i+3​∑n=1Nan​∂y−1(ψ1​n​ψ2​n​x−ψ2​n​ψ1​n​x)​ψ2​i​x.\displaystyle\hskip-42.67912pt\psi_{2it}=-\psi_{2ixxx}+3\sum^{N}_{n=1}a_{n}\partial^{-1}_{y}(\psi_{1n}\psi_{2n})_{xx}\psi_{2i}+3\sum^{N}_{n=1}a_{n}\partial^{-1}_{y}(\psi_{1n}\psi_{2nx}-\psi_{2n}\psi_{1nx})\psi_{2ix}. (4.29)

Taking N=1N=1, a1=1a_{1}=1, ψ10=ψ1,ψ20=ψ2\psi_{10}=\psi_{1},\psi_{20}=\psi_{2}, the system (4.29) becomes

ψ1​t=−ψ1​x​x​x+3​ψ1​∂y−1(ψ1​ψ2)x​x−3​ψ1​x​∂y−1(ψ1​ψ2​x−ψ2​ψ1​x),\displaystyle\psi_{1t}=-\psi_{1xxx}+3\psi_{1}\partial^{-1}_{y}(\psi_{1}\psi_{2})_{xx}-3\psi_{1x}\partial^{-1}_{y}(\psi_{1}\psi_{2x}-\psi_{2}\psi_{1x}),
ψ2​t=−ψ2​x​x​x+3​ψ2​∂y−1(ψ1​ψ2)x​x+3​ψ2​x​∂y−1(ψ1​ψ2​x−ψ2​ψ1​x).\displaystyle\psi_{2t}=-\psi_{2xxx}+3\psi_{2}\partial^{-1}_{y}(\psi_{1}\psi_{2})_{xx}+3\psi_{2x}\partial^{-1}_{y}(\psi_{1}\psi_{2x}-\psi_{2}\psi_{1x}). (4.30)

For ψ1=ψ2\psi_{1}=\psi_{2}, y=xy=x, system (4.30) reduces to the mKdV equation. So we call system (4.30) a coupled modified ANNV equation.

5 Conclusions and discussions

In this paper, we pay close attention to nonlocal symmetries of the HS-cKdV system from DT and their applications. Some important and meaningful results are obtained.

In general, to search for nonlocal symmetries is an interesting but difficult work. Here, starting from the known DT of the HS-cKdV system, some different types of nonlocal symmetries are derived directly. Besides, infinitely many nonlocal symmetries can be obtained by introducing some internal parameters from the seed symmetry.

Our next objective is focused on how to localize the nonlocal symmetry related to the DT. In fact, for some given nonlocal symmetries of the differential equation(s), whether these symmetries can be transformed to local ones is still unknown. Fortunately, through introducing five potentials, the nonlocal symmetry obtained from the DT is successfully localized to some local ones in our paper. This procedure leads the original HS-cKdV system to be extend the prolonged system. In particular, using the Lie’s first theorem to these local symmetries, one can find that the corresponding finite symmetry transformations have different group parameters from the initial DT but possess the same infinitesimal forms. Meanwhile, we also observe the fact that the DT of the HS-cKdV system is closely related to the Möbious transformation of its Schwartz form.

For the prolonged system, the general Lie symmetry transformations and the corresponding similarity reductions are considered. Some novel exact solutions of the HS-cKdV system are presented, which imply several classes of exact interaction solutions among solitons and other complicated waves including periodic cnoidal waves, Painlevé waves and rational waves. Actually, it is very difficult to obtain these types of solutions from the original DT by solving the spectral problem directly. The reason lies that to solve the spectral problem with the seed solution being taken non-constant and non-soliton solutions is not an easy work usually. Therefore, a simple alternative way is provided to construct some new solutions for the integrable models with the known DT.

The left work of this paper is to extend the HS-cKdV system to some new integrable models from the nonlocal symmetry related to the DT in two aspects. In fact, the existence of infinitely many symmetries suggests the existence of integrable hierarchies. By introducing the internal parameter, the negative HS-cKdV hierarchy is obtained without the inverse of the known recursion operator. Using a Miura transformation, this hierarchy is transformed to a coupled sinh-Gordon hierarchy. In addition, symmetry constraint approach is one of the most powerful tools to give one new integrable models from known ones. Usually, using this method, one obtains the lower dimensional integrable models from higher ones. Here, both lower and higher dimensional integrable models are presented by means of the symmetry constraints.

Using the DT to search for nonlocal symmetries of integrable models and then applying them to construct exact solutions and new integrable models are both of considerable interest. However, the concrete integrability for the given lower and higher dimensional models is unknown. Moreover, in Ref[19], Lou et al. had made use of the multi-DT to obtain some interesting nonlocal symmetries and constructed various lower and higher dimensional integrable models. Now a natural problem is how to use those nonlocal symmetries related to the multi-DT to obtain more novel solutions. These matters are worthy of further study.
